title: How Sleep Pills Mute Your Brain's Night Wash
description:
During natural deep sleep, the brainstem releases gentle waves of norepinephrine roughly every fifty seconds. Each slow pulse squeezes and relaxes cerebral blood vessels like a sponge pump, pushing clear fluid through brain tissue to wash out daily waste.

When scientists compared natural sleep against the common prescription sleep aid zolpidem, subjects fell asleep fast yet saw slow pump waves drop by fifty percent and fluid transport fall by thirty percent. Two-day human brain dye scans also showed that skipping one night of sleep stalls cleanup across eighty-five regions.

Research: Hauglund, Nedergaard et al., University of Copenhagen and University of Oxford (2025), and Eide et al. (2021).
pinned_comment: Do you wake up clearer after natural sleep, or have sleep aids ever left your morning head feeling heavy?
